parameter_state.description: What one parameter of the spec came to in this document. Every other state in this file belongs to a row, so a parameter that produced no row left no byte at all and "the document does not carry it" and "it was never asked" were the same empty file.

parameter.description: The spec's uri for the parameter, the same key a tuple carries.

x-doc.exhausted: no value, and the run did not finish this document. Document-wide: there is no per-parameter run signal, so a truncated run marks every unanswered parameter exhausted together
x-doc.read: at least one value of this parameter was read and accepted
x-doc.unbacked: no value survived, and at least one was refused. A finding about the model or about the passages, not about the document
x-doc.unstated: no value and nothing refused: the document was read and does not carry this parameter. The one of the four that is a finding about the document rather than about the run

block_id.description: Placeholder of the item in that section, e.g. p85_tbl0.

document_id.description: Documents.id. What the serializer joins from the database to mint the document's IRI is not carried here: which columns those are is the profile's business, not the row's.

image.description: Crop path relative to the image root.

parent_section.description: Sections.id of the section a table or figure stands in.

rects.description: Highlight boxes on the page, when the passage could be located.

title.description: The section title, or a table's or figure's caption, resolved to the sentence before its placeholder where the stored caption is a footnote.

via.description: How this source reached the window: a retrieval probe, or 'parent' for the section a table stands in.

claim.description: The claim as the model returned it. A sentinel carries _harvest_failed with _why: the server was gone, it answered 429 or 5xx, the model answered nothing, or the reply did not fit and there was nothing left to split. A hole of a reading also carries _parameter, the parameter the passage was to be read for.

parameter.description: The spec parameter, or whatever the claim named.

anyOf.pattern: ^claim names no parameter of the spec$
^a (text|category) parameter needs a non-empty string value$
^axis '.*': .* (not in vocabulary and axis is required|is not an integer|not in enum .*)$
^quote missing or too short to identify anything$
^quote not found in the source it cites$
^value .* does not occur in the quote$
^value .* does not follow from its inputs$

reason.description: Why the claim was refused; one of the reason families of verify.py and pipeline.py.

x-doc.derived: not asked: the spec decides this coordinate from something already on the row (the unit), or the request names it (the parameter of a row read for one field)
x-doc.exhausted: still open when the window budget ended with the document unread. A finding about the run
x-doc.out_of_slice: never asked: a gate coordinate (the profile's SLICE) had already put the row outside what this run serializes
x-doc.read: answered, and the cited passage carries the answer
x-doc.unanswered: the field reply never mentioned this row. A finding about the model
x-doc.unbacked: answered, but no shown passage carried the answer, or the passage belonged to another row, and no later window fixed it
x-doc.unstated: answered: the passages shown do not state it. A finding about the document, and only final once the sweep ran out of it

summary.description: The last line of the file: how this document's own values are distributed. A contested identity is decided by the serializer and a second reading is a later pass, so neither is counted here. The levels are a floor, and the graph side recomputes them. A pass that appended a parameter built this line again over every tuple and refusal the file holds; the refusals of the first pass are counted as they were stored and are not revisited, so a value refused then for want of that parameter stays in the count.

image_origin.description: Values read out of a table or figure image rather than the document's text.

levels.description: How many values reached each level.

x-doc.A: read off its own passage, in the document's own text
x-doc.B: the same, but out of an image transcription or a page a model transcribed
x-doc.C: a coordinate was not read; see reasons
x-doc.D: something speaks against the reading; see reasons

reasons.description: Why values are not an A, counted. A closed list: a reason nobody can enumerate is a reason nobody can count.

unlisted_units.description: The units numbers were read with that are no entry of their parameter's list, as the plan prints them, counted: read and not converted, until the list grows and a top-up asks them again (owner decision 2026-11-07). Absent in a file written before.

aggregation.description: Axis 'aggregation' of Gebäudeanzahl. A closed list; an entry beginning 'out:' is a deliberate non-class answer and mints no node. null unless aggregation_state is 'read' or 'derived'.

x-kg.label: has aggregation type
x-kg.note: Object is a named individual of OEO_00140068 aggregation type. Derived from the unit, never asked: a number of buildings is a stock at one point in time.

arithmetic mean.meaning: Durchschnittswert, berechnet als arithmetisches Mittel über Datensätze.

instantaneous.meaning: Wert, der exakt zu einem zeitlichen Nullpunkt gemessen oder modelliert wird.

integral.meaning: Summe oder Integral von Werten innerhalb eines Zeitraums oder Gebiets, etwa eine Jahressumme, der Normalfall.
spellings: Summe oder Integral über einen Zeitraum oder ein Gebiet

maximum.meaning: Höchster Wert innerhalb einer Menge von Datenwerten in einem Bereich.

minimum.meaning: Niedrigster Wert innerhalb einer Menge von Datenwerten in einem Bereich.

aggregation.x-question: Wie fasst diese Zahl Werte über Zeit oder Raum zusammen?

aggregation_link_quote.description: Only with window `base_year` or `target_year`: the passage where the row names that state ('aggregation_raw'). 'aggregation_quote' is then the frame's passage that prints the number.

aggregation_means.description: The entries of the document's list of names (its scenarios, its works) 'aggregation' means: the entry its name is, or the entry of each member where its words name a group; empty where they name a group the field takes no members for, or where the request found they name no such thing (owner decision 2026-11-09). The graph writes the row to each of them, an empty list to none.

aggregation_producer.description: Who re-read 'aggregation': the position of its entry in the `producers` list of the stamp beside the harvest. Written by a top-up for each coordinate it re-read, and by a pass that appended a parameter for each coordinate of the rows it wrote, never by the harvest, so a missing key means the harvest read it. A position the stamp has no entry for (the stamps were deleted) means nobody can say. Recorded and never compared.

aggregation_quote.description: The verbatim passage carrying 'aggregation'. Present exactly when aggregation_state is 'read'.

aggregation_raw.description: The document's own wording 'aggregation' was read from. This is what a later re-mapping onto a changed vocabulary works on, so a choice without it is counted (raw_missing).

aggregation_raw_foreign.description: The wording does not name the option chosen for 'aggregation': the model mapped a word the spec does not list onto this class. Kept and counted, not refused: some of those mappings are right.

aggregation_seen.description: A wording the model noticed for 'aggregation' while answering 'not stated', or offered as an answer the closed list does not hold. Vocabulary review material, never evidence.

aggregation_source.description: Which source the passage for 'aggregation' was found in. How far that may be from the row is the axis' own rule (own | local | any).

aggregation_state.description: How the coordinate 'aggregation' ended. Always present: a missing key and a refused reading must not look alike.

aggregation_window.description: [stage, index] of the window 'aggregation' was read in. `own`: at the value's own place, its row with its table's title and head or its sentence with the sentences beside it. `near`: in the pieces right before and after it. `found`: in the pieces a search found for the sentence of how the plan would print it. `piece`: a work read once for the value's piece, the line that names it or shows the piece is this publication's own. `entry`: the work of the entry of the document's list the value's name is. `plan_years`: a year none of these found, read from the plan's base and target years in a request of its own. The other stages are those of harvests made before the reading in pieces: `frame` is the one that is not a window: the coordinate was read ONCE for the document and applied to this row, and the index is which of the document's pairs it came from. `base_year`: the row's passage names the document's base state by word, and the index is the pair whose quote prints the number. `target_year`: the same for the document's target. `table`: read once for the row's table and taken by this row. `head`: the year the head of the row's column prints, one of the document's pairs, taken off the table and not asked; the index is the column. `retrieval`, `rest` and `places` are the windows of the reading by passages.

at.description: Where the value stands (owner decisions 2026-11-08): its passage, the number of its line there, the cell of a table row, and the last line of a value over several lines. The quote is that line.

carrier.description: Axis 'carrier' of Gebäudeanzahl. A closed list; an entry beginning 'out:' is a deliberate non-class answer and mints no node. null unless carrier_state is 'read' or 'derived'.

x-kg.label: refers to energy carrier
x-kg.note: Object is an OEO class (punning). The predicate is the MHPKG schema's slot, read from mhpkg_schema.yaml at serialization: refers to energy carrier. Its range is energy carrier, and the classes in outside_root are not under it in OEO; they are written all the same and counted, as input for the carrier axioms the ontology side is adding.

Kerosin.meaning:
Kerosene, also known as paraffin, lamp oil, and coal oil (an obsolete term), is a portion of matter consisting of combustible hydrocarbon liquid which is derived from petroleum. It is widely used as a fuel in industry as well as households. It is sometimes spelled kerosine in scientific and industrial usage.
[...]

Kerosene is widely used to power jet engines of aircraft (jet fuel) and some rocket engines and is also commonly used as a cooking and lighting fuel and for fire toys such as poi. In parts of Asia, kerosene is sometimes used as fuel for small outboard motors or even motorcycles.

Stadtgas.meaning:
Gasworks gas is manufactured coal based gas that covers all types of gases produced in public utility or private plants, whose main purpose is manufacture, transport and distribution of gas. It includes gas produced by carbonisation (including gas produced by coke ovens and transferred to gasworks gas), by total gasification with or without enrichment with oil products (LPG, residual fuel oil, etc.), and by reforming and simple mixing of gases and/or air, reported under the rows ‘from other sources’. Under the transformation sector identify amounts of gasworks gas transferred to blended natural gas which will be distributed and consumed through the natural gas grid.

The production of other coal gases (i.e. coke oven gas, blast furnace gas and oxygen steel furnace gas) should be reported in the columns concerning such gases, and not as production of gasworks gas. The coal gases transferred to gasworks plants should then be reported (in their own column) in the transformation sector in the gasworks plants row. The total amount of gasworks gas resulting from transfers of other coal gases should appear in the production line for gasworks gas.

parameter.x-description-source: Eine im Wärmeplan angegebene Zahl von Gebäuden, je Energieträger, Heizungsart, Sektor, Gebiet und Jahr. Die MHPO definiert sie so: building count ist "A building count is a quantity value that measures the number of buildings in a building stock.". Gezählt werden nur Gebäude: eine Zahl von Wohnungen, Anschlüssen, Anlagen, Heizungen oder Einwohnern ist keine Gebäudeanzahl. Eine Angabe je Gebäude (MWh je Gebäude) ist eine Energiemenge und keine Gebäudeanzahl.
parameter.x-question: Um WELCHE Kennzahl handelt es sich bei dieser Zahl? Entscheide danach, was die Quelle über sie sagt: die Einheit, die Spalten- oder Zeilenbeschriftung und die Tabellen- oder Abschnittsüberschrift. Eine Angabe in t CO2 ist eine Emission, eine Angabe in MWh oder GWh ein Energieverbrauch. Zitiere die Stelle, aus der das hervorgeht. Eine Angabe in kW, MW oder GW ist eine Leistung. Eine Angabe in % ist ein Anteil. Eine Zahl von Gebäuden ist eine Gebäudeanzahl.

Ammoniak.meaning: Ammonia is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NH3. It has a gaseous normal state of matter and can act as an air pollutant. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

B7.meaning: B7 is a diesel fuel that consists of fossil diesel fuel and up to 7 % biodiesel and that is liquid.

Benzin.meaning: Gasoline (American English) or petrol (British English) is a portion of matter in the form of a transparent petroleum-derived liquid that is used primarily as a fuel in spark-ignited internal combustion engines. It consists mostly of organic compounds obtained by the fractional distillation of petroleum, enhanced with a variety of additives.

Bio-Ottokraftstoff.meaning: Biogasoline is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a gasoline fuel role. It consists of bioethanol, biomethanol and products of these two substances. It is made from vegetable or animal material and thus has a biogenic origin.

Biobrennstoff.meaning: A biofuel is a combustion fuel that has a biogenic origin.

Biodiesel.meaning: Biodiesel is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a diesel fuel role. It is produced from plants or animals and thus has a biogenic origin.

Bioethanol.meaning: Bioethanol is ethanol with a biogenic origin.

Biogas.meaning: Biogas: Durch anaerobe Vergärung entstehendes Gasgemisch aus hauptsächlich Methan und Kohlendioxid, das als Brennstoff dient.

Biomasse.meaning: Biomasse: Stoff pflanzlichen oder tierischen Ursprungs und damit biogener Herkunft.

Biomethan.meaning: Biomethan: Aus Biogas durch Abtrennung von Kohlendioxid gewonnenes Gasgemisch aus hauptsächlich Methan, das als Brennstoff dient.

Braunkohle.meaning: Braunkohle: Nicht backende Kohle mit einem Brennwert unter 17 435 kJ/kg und über 31 % flüchtigen Bestandteilen.

Brennstoff.meaning: A fuel is a portion of matter that has the disposition to be an energy carrier and that has a fuel role.

Brent-Rohöl.meaning: Brent crude is a crude oil that is extracted in the North Sea and traded at ICE London.

Dampf.meaning: Steam is water that has a gaseous state of matter.

Dieselkraftstoff.meaning: A diesel fuel is a combustion fuel that has a diesel fuel role.

Druckgaskraftstoff.meaning: A compressed gas fuel is a combustion fuel that has a compressed gas fuel role.

Druckluft.meaning: Compressed air is air that has been compressed to store energy. To discharge energy, the air is expanded.

Düsenkraftstoff.meaning: Jet fuel is kerosene used for aviation turbine power units. It has the same distillation characteristics between 150 °C and 300 °C (generally not above 250 °C) and flash point as kerosene. In addition, it has particular specifications (such as freezing point) which are established by the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

E10.meaning: E10 is a gasoline fuel that consists of (fossil) gasoline and up to 10 % ethanol and that is liquid.

Elektrolysewasserstoff.meaning: Electrolytic hydrogen is hydrogen that is a physical output of a water electrolysis process.

Elektrolysewasserstoff aus Kernenergie.meaning: Nuclear electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with nuclear electrical energy.

Elektrolysewasserstoff aus Solarstrom.meaning: Solar electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with solar electrical energy.

Endenergieträger.meaning: A final energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the disposition final energy carrier disposition.

Erdgas.meaning: Erdgas: Gasgemisch aus unterirdischen Lagerstätten, das hauptsächlich aus Methan besteht.

Erdgas aus reinen Gasfeldern.meaning: Non associated gas is natural gas originating from fields producing hydrocarbons only in gaseous form.

Erdölbegleitgas.meaning: Associated gas is a natural gas that is a byproduct from crude oil exploitation.

Ethanol.meaning: Ethanol is a portion of matter with the chemical formula C2H6O. It has a liquid normal state of matter and can be used as a combustion fuel.

Ethen.meaning: Ethene, or colloquially Ethylene, is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula H2C=CH2. It is gaseous in its normal state and can be used as a combustion fuel.

Fernwärme.meaning: Fernwärme: Leitungsgebundene Wärmelieferung an Wohn- oder Gewerbegebäude.

Flugbenzin.meaning: Aviation gasoline is gasoline used as motor spirit and prepared especially for aviation piston engines, with an octane number suited to the engine, a freezing point of -60 °C and a distillation range usually within the limits of 30 °C and 180 °C.

Fluss.meaning: A river is a water body that moves through permanent or seasonal flow process from elevated land towards lower elevations through a definite channel and empties either into a sea, lake, or another river or ends on land as bed seepage and evapotranspiration exceed water supply.

Flüssiggas.meaning: Flüssiggasgemisch aus Propan und Butan, unterscheidet sich als fossiler Gasbrennstoff.

Flüssigluft.meaning: Liquid air is air that has a liquid state of matter.

Gas aus Kohle.meaning: A manufactured coal based gas is a gas mixture that is manufactured from coal. It is used as fossil fuel.

Gasöl.meaning: Gas/diesel oil is a portion of matter that is primarily a medium distillate distilling between 180 °C and 380 °C. Includes blending components. Several grades are available depending on uses.

Geothermie.meaning: Geothermie: Wärmeenergie, die aus dem Inneren der Erdkruste freigesetzt wird.

Gestein.meaning: A rock is a portion of matter that is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter that is part of the earth's crust.

Gewässer.meaning: A water body is an accumulation of liquid water of varying size on the surface of the Earth.

Gichtgas.meaning: Blast furnace gas is manufactured coal based gas produced during the combustion of coke in blast furnaces in the iron and steel industry. It is recovered and used as a fuel partly within the plant and partly in other steel industry processes or in power stations equipped to burn it. The quantity of fuel should be reported on a gross calorific value basis.

Grubengas.meaning: Colliery gas is natural gas found in coal mines (British English: colliery). The main component is methane. Synonyms are firedamp, mine gas. It is used as a fossil fuel.

Heizöl.meaning: Heizöl: Gasöl für industrielle und gewerbliche Zwecke, auch schwere Gasöle, die als petrochemische Rohstoffe dienen.

Holz.meaning: Holz: Biomasse von Bäumen in festem Aggregatzustand, die als Brennstoff genutzt werden kann.

Holzkohle.meaning: Charcoal is a portion of matter produced from wood via pyrolysis. It has a solid state of matter and can be used as fuel.

Industrieabfallbrennstoff.meaning: An industrial waste fuel is waste fuel produced by industry.

Kernbrennstoff.meaning: A nuclear fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by undergoing nuclear fission.

Kerosin.meaning:
Kerosene, also known as paraffin, lamp oil, and coal oil (an obsolete term), is a portion of matter consisting of combustible hydrocarbon liquid which is derived from petroleum. It is widely used as a fuel in industry as well as households. It is sometimes spelled kerosine in scientific and industrial usage.
[...]

Kerosene is widely used to power jet engines of aircraft (jet fuel) and some rocket engines and is also commonly used as a cooking and lighting fuel and for fire toys such as poi. In parts of Asia, kerosene is sometimes used as fuel for small outboard motors or even motorcycles.

Kohle.meaning: Kohle: Brennbares schwarzes bis schwarzbraunes Sedimentgestein, das in Flözen entstanden ist.

Kohleabraum.meaning: Coal refuse is a fossil waste fuel that is the material left over from coal mining. It can partially be reused as fuel.

Kohlenwasserstoff.meaning: Hydrocarbon is a portion of matter which is member of class of organic chemical compounds composed only of the elements carbon (C) and hydrogen (H).

Kokereigas.meaning: Coke oven gas is manufactured coal based gas obtained as a by-product of the manufacture of coke oven coke for the production of iron and steel.

Kokskohle.meaning: Coking coal is hard coal that is bituminous with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is greater than 23 865 kJ/kg (5 700 kcal/kg) on an ash-free but moist basis.

Luft.meaning: Air is a gas mixture that forms the Earth's atmosphere.

Methan.meaning: Methane is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH4. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It occurs naturally in the atmosphere as a trace gas and can work as a greenhouse gas. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Methanol.meaning: Methanol is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH3OH. It has a liquid normal state of matter. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Mineralöl.meaning: A mineral oil is a fossil combustion fuel that is either crude oil or a mineral oil product.

Mineralölprodukt.meaning: A mineral oil product is a fossil combustion fuel produced in a mineral oil refining process.

Mischkraftstoff.meaning: A blended liquid fuel is a liquid combustion fuel that contains a liquid fossil fuel and a liquid renewable fuel or a liquid biofuel.

Motorenbenzin.meaning:
Motor gasoline is gasoline consisting of a mixture of light hydrocarbons distilling between 35 °C and 215 °C. It is used as a fuel for land based spark ignition engines. Motor gasoline may include additives, oxygenates and octane enhancers, including lead compounds such as TEL and TML.

Includes motor gasoline blending components (excluding additives/oxygenates), e.g. alkylates, isomerate, reformate, cracked gasoline destined for use as finished motor gasoline.

Ottokraftstoff.meaning: A gasoline fuel is a combustion fuel that has a gasoline fuel role.

Ozean.meaning: The ocean is a water body that consists of salt water and is covering approximately 71% of Earth's surface.

Petrolkoks.meaning: Petroleum coke is a portion of matter with a solid state of matter that is produced in a mineral oil refining process. It consists mainly of carbon and can be uses as a fuel.

Photon.meaning: A photon is a material entity that is a light particle.

Plutonium.meaning: Plutonium is a portion of matter with the chemical formula Pu. It has a solid normal state of matter.

Primärenergieträger.meaning: A primary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the disposition primary energy carrier disposition.

PtL-Kraftstoff.meaning: PtL fuel is a liquid synthetic fuel produced in a power-to-liquid system from water and carbon dioxide using electrical energy.

Raffineriegas.meaning: Refinery gas is a gas mixture that is produced as a by-product of a mineral oil refining process. It mainly consists of hydrogen, methane, ethane and olefins and can be used as a fuel.

Rohöl.meaning: Crude oil is a portion of mater of fossil origin comprising a mixture of hydrocarbons and associated impurities, such as sulphur. It exists in the liquid phase under normal surface temperature and pressure and its physical characteristics (density, viscosity, etc.) are highly variable. This category includes field or lease condensate recovered from associated and non-associated gas where it is commingled with the commercial crude oil stream.

Sekundärenergieträger.meaning: A secondary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the secondary energy carrier disposition.

Siedlungsabfälle.meaning: Siedlungsabfälle: Abfallbrennstoff aus Haushalten oder nicht-industriellen gewerblichen Tätigkeiten.

Solarthermie.meaning: Solarthermie: Wärmeenergie, die als Ergebnis einer solarthermischen Energieumwandlung entsteht.

Sonstige.meaning: Etwas, das keiner der übrigen Einträge dieser Liste ist.

Stadtgas.meaning:
Gasworks gas is manufactured coal based gas that covers all types of gases produced in public utility or private plants, whose main purpose is manufacture, transport and distribution of gas. It includes gas produced by carbonisation (including gas produced by coke ovens and transferred to gasworks gas), by total gasification with or without enrichment with oil products (LPG, residual fuel oil, etc.), and by reforming and simple mixing of gases and/or air, reported under the rows ‘from other sources’. Under the transformation sector identify amounts of gasworks gas transferred to blended natural gas which will be distributed and consumed through the natural gas grid.

The production of other coal gases (i.e. coke oven gas, blast furnace gas and oxygen steel furnace gas) should be reported in the columns concerning such gases, and not as production of gasworks gas. The coal gases transferred to gasworks plants should then be reported (in their own column) in the transformation sector in the gasworks plants row. The total amount of gasworks gas resulting from transfers of other coal gases should appear in the production line for gasworks gas.

Steinkohle.meaning: Steinkohle: Kohle mit einem Brennwert über 23 865 kJ/kg und einer mittleren Vitrinitreflexion von mindestens 0,6.

Strom.meaning: Elektrische Energie aus geladenen Teilchen, unterscheidet sich als nicht-materieller Energieträger.

Summe.meaning: Die Zahl gilt für alle Energieträger zusammen: ihre Zeile oder Spalte summiert ausdrücklich über die Energieträger, oder ihre eigene Tabelle oder ihr Satz ist gar nicht nach Energieträgern aufgeteilt, nur nach anderem (Gebäudetyp, Sektor, Gebiet). Der Wärmebedarf der Gebäude eines Gebiets bleibt Summe, solange die Stelle nicht nach Energieträgern aufteilt.

Synthesegas.meaning: Syngas is a gas mixture consisting primarily of hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and very often carbon dioxide, that can be used as fuel.

Thorium.meaning: Thorium is a portion of matter with the chemical formula Th. It has a solid normal state of matter.

Torf.meaning: Peat is a or portion of matter that is a soft, porous or compressed, sedimentary deposit of plant origin with high water content (up to 90 % in the raw state) and can be used as combustion fuel. As the natural formation of peat takes at least centuries, peat is usually considered having a fossil origin.

Umweltwärme.meaning: In Luft, Erde oder Wasser gespeicherte Wärme, die durch Wärmepumpen genutzt wird.

Uran.meaning: Uranium is a portion of matter that has the atomic number 92. It is a silver-grey metal.

Verbrennungsbrennstoff.meaning: A combustion fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by chemical reaction with other substances.

Wasser.meaning: Water is a portion of matter with the chemical formula H2O. It has a liquid normal state of matter.

Wasserstoff.meaning: Wasserstoff: Stoff mit der chemischen Formel H2, der gasförmig vorliegt und als Brennstoff verwendet werden kann.

Wasserstoff aus Dampfreformierung.meaning: Steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is a physical output of a steam reforming process.

Wasserstoff aus Dampfreformierung mit CO.meaning: Abated steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is output of a steam reforming process which is followed by a carbon capture and storage process.

Wasserstoff aus Methanpyrolyse.meaning: Methane pyrolytic hydrogen is synthetic hydrogen that is produced from pyrolysis of methane and solid CO2 storage.

West Texas Intermediate.meaning: Western Texas Intermediate (WTI) is a crude oil that is extracted on US territory and traded at NYMEX New York.

anthropogene Umweltwärme.meaning: Umweltwärme mit anthropogenem Ursprung, unterscheidet sich durch menschliche Entstehung.

biogener Abfallbrennstoff.meaning: Abfallbrennstoff mit biogenem Ursprung, unterscheidet sich als spezifische Abfallart.

biogener Festbrennstoff.meaning: Biogener Festbrennstoff: Organisches, nicht fossiles Material biologischen Ursprungs, das zur Wärme- oder Stromerzeugung genutzt werden kann.

biogener Industrieabfallbrennstoff.meaning: A biogenic industrial waste fuel is an industrial waste fuel that has a biogenic origin.

biogener Siedlungsabfall.meaning: Siedlungsabfall mit biogenem Ursprung, unterscheidet sich durch die biologische Herkunft.

erneuerbarer Brennstoff.meaning: A renewable fuel is a fuel that has a renewable origin and an renewable energy carrier disposition

erneuerbarer Elektrolysewasserstoff.meaning: Renewable electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with renewable electrical energy.

erneuerbarer Energieträger.meaning: A renewable energy carrier is an energy carrier that has a renewable energy carrier disposition.

fester Brennstoff.meaning: A solid combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

fester erneuerbarer Brennstoff.meaning: A solid renewable fuel is a renewable fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

fester fossiler Brennstoff.meaning: A solid fossil fuel is a fossil fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiger Biobrennstoff.meaning: A liquid biofuel is a biofuel that has liquid as its normal state of matter.

flüssiger Brennstoff.meaning: A liquid combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiger Wasserstoff.meaning: Liquid hydrogen is hydrogen that has been brought to a liquid state of matter at -253°C.

flüssiger erneuerbarer Brennstoff.meaning: A liquid renewable fuel is a renewable fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiger fossiler Brennstoff.meaning: A liquid fossil fuel is a fossil combustion fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiger synthetischer Brennstoff.meaning: A liquid synthetic fuel is a synthetic fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiges Wasser.meaning: Liquid water is water that has a liquid state of matter.

fossiler Abfallbrennstoff.meaning: A fossil waste fuel is a waste fuel that has a fossil origin.

fossiler Brennstoff.meaning: A fossil combustion fuel is a combustion fuel with the origin fossil.

fossiler Dieselkraftstoff.meaning: Diesel fuel is gas diesel oil used on-road for diesel compression ignition (cars, trucks, etc.), usually of low sulphur content.

fossiler Industrieabfallbrennstoff.meaning: A fossil industrial waste fuel is an industrial waste fuel that has a fossil origin.

fossiler Siedlungsabfall.meaning: A fossil municipal waste fuel is an municipal waste fuel that has a fossil origin.

fossiler Wasserstoff.meaning: Fossil hydrogen is hydrogen with fossil origin.

fossiler Wasserstoff aus Dampfreformieru.meaning: Fossil steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is produced from a fossil combustion fuel in a steam reforming process which is not followed by a carbon capture and storage process.

gasförmiger Brennstoff.meaning: A gaseous combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a gaseous state of matter under normal conditions.

gasförmiger erneuerbarer Brennstoff.meaning: A gaseous renewable fuel is a renewable fuel that has a gaseous state of matter under normal conditions.

gasförmiger fossiler Brennstoff.meaning: A gaseous fossil fuel is a fossil combustion fuel that has a gaseous state of matter under normal conditions.

hochgepumptes Wasser.meaning: Pumped water is liquid water which was pumped into an upper reservoir and thus contains potential energy.

industrielle Abwärme.meaning: Industrielle Abwärme: Abwärme, die als Energieausgabe eines industriellen Prozesses entsteht.

komprimiertes Biomethan.meaning: Compressed biomethane is biomethane that has been compressed.

komprimiertes Erdgas (CNG).meaning: Compressed natural gas (CNG) is natural gas that has been compressed.

komprimiertes synthetisches Methan.meaning: Compressed synthetic methane is synthetic methane that has been compressed.

landwirtschaftlicher Abfallbrennstoff.meaning: Landwirtschaftlicher Abfallbrennstoff: Abfallbrennstoff aus der Landwirtschaft.

nachhaltiger Biobrennstoff.meaning: A sustainable biofuel is a biofuel that does conform to sustainability criteria.

natürliche Umweltwärme.meaning: Umweltwärme mit erneuerbarem Ursprung, unterscheidet sich durch natürliche Herkunft.

nicht nachhaltiger Biobrennstoff.meaning: A non-sustainable biofuel is a biofuel that does not conform to sustainability criteria.

spaltbares Material.meaning: A fissile material entity is a material entity that has the disposition to carry nuclear (binding) energy.

subbituminöse Kohle.meaning: Sub bituminous coal is coal that is non-agglomerating with a gross calorific value between 17 435 kJ/kg (4 165 kcal/kg) and 23 865 kJ/kg (5 700 kcal/kg) containing more than 31 % volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.

synthetische Gase.meaning: Synthetische Gase: Synthetischer Brennstoff, der unter Normalbedingungen gasförmig ist.

synthetischer Brennstoff.meaning: A synthetic fuel is a fuel produced from one or more portion(s) of matter using electric energy.

synthetischer Wasserstoff.meaning: Synthetic hydrogen is hydrogen with synthetic origin.

synthetisches Ammoniak.meaning: Synthetic ammonia is ammonia that has a synthetic origin.

synthetisches Methan.meaning: Synthetic methane is methane that has a synthetic origin.

verflüssigtes Erdgas (LNG).meaning: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is natural gas that has a liquid state of matter.

carrier_means.description: The entries of the document's list of names (its scenarios, its works) 'carrier' means: the entry its name is, or the entry of each member where its words name a group; empty where they name a group the field takes no members for, or where the request found they name no such thing (owner decision 2026-11-09). The graph writes the row to each of them, an empty list to none.

carrier_producer.description: Who re-read 'carrier': the position of its entry in the `producers` list of the stamp beside the harvest. Written by a top-up for each coordinate it re-read, and by a pass that appended a parameter for each coordinate of the rows it wrote, never by the harvest, so a missing key means the harvest read it. A position the stamp has no entry for (the stamps were deleted) means nobody can say. Recorded and never compared.

carrier_raw.description: The document's own wording 'carrier' was read from. This is what a later re-mapping onto a changed vocabulary works on, so a choice without it is counted (raw_missing).

carrier_raw_foreign.description: The wording does not name the option chosen for 'carrier': the model mapped a word the spec does not list onto this class. Kept and counted, not refused: some of those mappings are right.

carrier_seen.description: A wording the model noticed for 'carrier' while answering 'not stated', or offered as an answer the closed list does not hold. Vocabulary review material, never evidence.

carrier_state.description: How the coordinate 'carrier' ended. Always present: a missing key and a refused reading must not look alike.

carrier_window.description: [stage, index] of the window 'carrier' was read in. `own`: at the value's own place, its row with its table's title and head or its sentence with the sentences beside it. `near`: in the pieces right before and after it. `found`: in the pieces a search found for the sentence of how the plan would print it. `piece`: a work read once for the value's piece, the line that names it or shows the piece is this publication's own. `entry`: the work of the entry of the document's list the value's name is. `plan_years`: a year none of these found, read from the plan's base and target years in a request of its own. The other stages are those of harvests made before the reading in pieces: `frame` is the one that is not a window: the coordinate was read ONCE for the document and applied to this row, and the index is which of the document's pairs it came from. `base_year`: the row's passage names the document's base state by word, and the index is the pair whose quote prints the number. `target_year`: the same for the document's target. `table`: read once for the row's table and taken by this row. `head`: the year the head of the row's column prints, one of the document's pairs, taken off the table and not asked; the index is the column. `retrieval`, `rest` and `places` are the windows of the reading by passages.

catalogue.description: The open catalogue record a value was looked up in, not read off the page: its source and id, what was searched, what it holds and which of its values matched the document's. The quote is the read value it was looked up with; the flag catalogue goes with it.

compute.description: The sandbox runs behind a computed value: {code, stdout, ok, error}, the last with the numbers it was worked out from (inputs) and what they make (expected).

computed.description: The value came out of the sandbox, not off the page; the quote proves the inputs it was computed from.

drawn.description: A figure's value only: whether its image only draws the number (a bar, a segment, an area, a point of a curve) rather than printing it, as the reading said. True sets the flag read_off.

flags.description: Non-fatal verifier findings. mapped:<axis>:<wording>-><uri> is the model mapping a word the spec does not list; period:* says whether a bare amount was shown to be a yearly one; review:* is what a second reading of this value under a narrower window came to, and only review:disagree is a reason.

head.description: The head of the table column the number stands in, as the plan prints it. Taken from the table, never asked. Absent where the number is no table cell or its column is not certain.

parameter.x-description-source: Eine im Wärmeplan bilanzierte Emissionsmenge, je Energieträger, Sektor und Jahr, oder ein Emissionsfaktor, die Emission je Einheit Aktivität, etwa g CO2/kWh. Welche Größe es ist, wählst du in "quantity" aus der Liste. Die Ontologie definiert die beiden Klassen so: CO2 emission value ist "a greenhouse gas emission value that quantifies a CO2 emission rate and has a mass unit", also reines Kohlendioxid. carbon dioxide equivalent quantity value ist "the combined effect of all emitted greenhouse gases by giving an equivalent amount of CO2", also alle Treibhausgase in CO2-Äquivalenten. Die Einheit verrät es meist: t CO2 gegen t CO2-Äq. Dazu stehen in der Liste die Oberklassen greenhouse gas emission value und emission value, wo die Stelle nicht sagt, welche Gase gemeint sind, und emission factor value, "a fraction value that quantifies an emission factor as quotient of the emissions or removals of a gas per unit activity". Die Einträge out: sind Größen ohne Klasse der Ontologie, etwa eine kumulierte Summe über mehrere Jahre, eine vermiedene Emission oder eine abgeschiedene Menge aus einer CCS-Anlage. Wähle den passenden davon, wenn die Zahl eine davon ist. Das ist ein richtiges Ergebnis, kein Fehler.
parameter.x-question: Um WELCHE Kennzahl handelt es sich bei dieser Zahl? Entscheide danach, was die Quelle über sie sagt: die Einheit, die Spalten- oder Zeilenbeschriftung und die Tabellen- oder Abschnittsüberschrift. Eine Angabe in t CO2 ist eine Emission, eine Angabe in MWh oder GWh ein Energieverbrauch. Zitiere die Stelle, aus der das hervorgeht. Eine Angabe in kW, MW oder GW ist eine Leistung. Eine Angabe in % ist ein Anteil. Eine Zahl von Gebäuden ist eine Gebäudeanzahl.

Ölheizung.meaning: Ölheizung: Verbrennungsbasierte Wärmeerzeugung unter Verwendung von Heizöl.

Abfallbrennstoff.meaning: Brennstoff, bei dem das Material Abfall ist, umfasst alle Abfallarten.

Abwärme.meaning: Abwärme: Wärmeenergie, die bei einem Energieumwandlungsprozess entsteht und ungenutzt an die Umwelt abgegeben wird.

Ammoniak.meaning: Ammonia is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NH3. It has a gaseous normal state of matter and can act as an air pollutant. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Anthrazit.meaning: Anthracite is a hard coal with a high caloric value due to its high carbon content (about 90 % fixed carbon).

B7.meaning: B7 is a diesel fuel that consists of fossil diesel fuel and up to 7 % biodiesel and that is liquid.

Benzin.meaning: Gasoline (American English) or petrol (British English) is a portion of matter in the form of a transparent petroleum-derived liquid that is used primarily as a fuel in spark-ignited internal combustion engines. It consists mostly of organic compounds obtained by the fractional distillation of petroleum, enhanced with a variety of additives.

Bio-Ottokraftstoff.meaning: Biogasoline is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a gasoline fuel role. It consists of bioethanol, biomethanol and products of these two substances. It is made from vegetable or animal material and thus has a biogenic origin.

Biobrennstoff.meaning: A biofuel is a combustion fuel that has a biogenic origin.

Biodiesel.meaning: Biodiesel is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a diesel fuel role. It is produced from plants or animals and thus has a biogenic origin.

Bioethanol.meaning: Bioethanol is ethanol with a biogenic origin.

Biogas.meaning: Biogas: Durch anaerobe Vergärung entstehendes Gasgemisch aus hauptsächlich Methan und Kohlendioxid, das als Brennstoff dient.

Biomasse.meaning: Biomasse: Stoff pflanzlichen oder tierischen Ursprungs und damit biogener Herkunft.

Biomethan.meaning: Biomethan: Aus Biogas durch Abtrennung von Kohlendioxid gewonnenes Gasgemisch aus hauptsächlich Methan, das als Brennstoff dient.

Braunkohle.meaning: Braunkohle: Nicht backende Kohle mit einem Brennwert unter 17 435 kJ/kg und über 31 % flüchtigen Bestandteilen.

Brennstoff.meaning: A fuel is a portion of matter that has the disposition to be an energy carrier and that has a fuel role.

Brent-Rohöl.meaning: Brent crude is a crude oil that is extracted in the North Sea and traded at ICE London.

Dampf.meaning: Steam is water that has a gaseous state of matter.

Dieselkraftstoff.meaning: A diesel fuel is a combustion fuel that has a diesel fuel role.

Druckgaskraftstoff.meaning: A compressed gas fuel is a combustion fuel that has a compressed gas fuel role.

Druckluft.meaning: Compressed air is air that has been compressed to store energy. To discharge energy, the air is expanded.

Düsenkraftstoff.meaning: Jet fuel is kerosene used for aviation turbine power units. It has the same distillation characteristics between 150 °C and 300 °C (generally not above 250 °C) and flash point as kerosene. In addition, it has particular specifications (such as freezing point) which are established by the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

E10.meaning: E10 is a gasoline fuel that consists of (fossil) gasoline and up to 10 % ethanol and that is liquid.

Elektrolysewasserstoff.meaning: Electrolytic hydrogen is hydrogen that is a physical output of a water electrolysis process.

Elektrolysewasserstoff aus Kernenergie.meaning: Nuclear electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with nuclear electrical energy.

Elektrolysewasserstoff aus Solarstrom.meaning: Solar electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with solar electrical energy.

Endenergieträger.meaning: A final energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the disposition final energy carrier disposition.

Erdgas.meaning: Erdgas: Gasgemisch aus unterirdischen Lagerstätten, das hauptsächlich aus Methan besteht.

Erdgas aus reinen Gasfeldern.meaning: Non associated gas is natural gas originating from fields producing hydrocarbons only in gaseous form.

Erdölbegleitgas.meaning: Associated gas is a natural gas that is a byproduct from crude oil exploitation.

Ethanol.meaning: Ethanol is a portion of matter with the chemical formula C2H6O. It has a liquid normal state of matter and can be used as a combustion fuel.

Ethen.meaning: Ethene, or colloquially Ethylene, is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula H2C=CH2. It is gaseous in its normal state and can be used as a combustion fuel.

Fernwärme.meaning: Fernwärme: Leitungsgebundene Wärmelieferung an Wohn- oder Gewerbegebäude.

Flugbenzin.meaning: Aviation gasoline is gasoline used as motor spirit and prepared especially for aviation piston engines, with an octane number suited to the engine, a freezing point of -60 °C and a distillation range usually within the limits of 30 °C and 180 °C.

Fluss.meaning: A river is a water body that moves through permanent or seasonal flow process from elevated land towards lower elevations through a definite channel and empties either into a sea, lake, or another river or ends on land as bed seepage and evapotranspiration exceed water supply.

Flüssiggas.meaning: Flüssiggasgemisch aus Propan und Butan, unterscheidet sich als fossiler Gasbrennstoff.

Flüssigluft.meaning: Liquid air is air that has a liquid state of matter.

Gas aus Kohle.meaning: A manufactured coal based gas is a gas mixture that is manufactured from coal. It is used as fossil fuel.

Gasöl.meaning: Gas/diesel oil is a portion of matter that is primarily a medium distillate distilling between 180 °C and 380 °C. Includes blending components. Several grades are available depending on uses.

Geothermie.meaning: Geothermie: Wärmeenergie, die aus dem Inneren der Erdkruste freigesetzt wird.

Gestein.meaning: A rock is a portion of matter that is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter that is part of the earth's crust.

Gewässer.meaning: A water body is an accumulation of liquid water of varying size on the surface of the Earth.

Gichtgas.meaning: Blast furnace gas is manufactured coal based gas produced during the combustion of coke in blast furnaces in the iron and steel industry. It is recovered and used as a fuel partly within the plant and partly in other steel industry processes or in power stations equipped to burn it. The quantity of fuel should be reported on a gross calorific value basis.

Grubengas.meaning: Colliery gas is natural gas found in coal mines (British English: colliery). The main component is methane. Synonyms are firedamp, mine gas. It is used as a fossil fuel.

Heizöl.meaning: Heizöl: Gasöl für industrielle und gewerbliche Zwecke, auch schwere Gasöle, die als petrochemische Rohstoffe dienen.

Holz.meaning: Holz: Biomasse von Bäumen in festem Aggregatzustand, die als Brennstoff genutzt werden kann.

Holzkohle.meaning: Charcoal is a portion of matter produced from wood via pyrolysis. It has a solid state of matter and can be used as fuel.

Industrieabfallbrennstoff.meaning: An industrial waste fuel is waste fuel produced by industry.

Kernbrennstoff.meaning: A nuclear fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by undergoing nuclear fission.

Kerosin.meaning:
Kerosene, also known as paraffin, lamp oil, and coal oil (an obsolete term), is a portion of matter consisting of combustible hydrocarbon liquid which is derived from petroleum. It is widely used as a fuel in industry as well as households. It is sometimes spelled kerosine in scientific and industrial usage.
[...]

Kerosene is widely used to power jet engines of aircraft (jet fuel) and some rocket engines and is also commonly used as a cooking and lighting fuel and for fire toys such as poi. In parts of Asia, kerosene is sometimes used as fuel for small outboard motors or even motorcycles.

Kohle.meaning: Kohle: Brennbares schwarzes bis schwarzbraunes Sedimentgestein, das in Flözen entstanden ist.

Kohleabraum.meaning: Coal refuse is a fossil waste fuel that is the material left over from coal mining. It can partially be reused as fuel.

Kohlenwasserstoff.meaning: Hydrocarbon is a portion of matter which is member of class of organic chemical compounds composed only of the elements carbon (C) and hydrogen (H).

Kokereigas.meaning: Coke oven gas is manufactured coal based gas obtained as a by-product of the manufacture of coke oven coke for the production of iron and steel.

Kokskohle.meaning: Coking coal is hard coal that is bituminous with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is greater than 23 865 kJ/kg (5 700 kcal/kg) on an ash-free but moist basis.

Luft.meaning: Air is a gas mixture that forms the Earth's atmosphere.

Methan.meaning: Methane is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH4. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It occurs naturally in the atmosphere as a trace gas and can work as a greenhouse gas. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Methanol.meaning: Methanol is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH3OH. It has a liquid normal state of matter. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Mineralöl.meaning: A mineral oil is a fossil combustion fuel that is either crude oil or a mineral oil product.

Mineralölprodukt.meaning: A mineral oil product is a fossil combustion fuel produced in a mineral oil refining process.

Mischkraftstoff.meaning: A blended liquid fuel is a liquid combustion fuel that contains a liquid fossil fuel and a liquid renewable fuel or a liquid biofuel.

Motorenbenzin.meaning:
Motor gasoline is gasoline consisting of a mixture of light hydrocarbons distilling between 35 °C and 215 °C. It is used as a fuel for land based spark ignition engines. Motor gasoline may include additives, oxygenates and octane enhancers, including lead compounds such as TEL and TML.

Includes motor gasoline blending components (excluding additives/oxygenates), e.g. alkylates, isomerate, reformate, cracked gasoline destined for use as finished motor gasoline.

Ottokraftstoff.meaning: A gasoline fuel is a combustion fuel that has a gasoline fuel role.

Ozean.meaning: The ocean is a water body that consists of salt water and is covering approximately 71% of Earth's surface.

Petrolkoks.meaning: Petroleum coke is a portion of matter with a solid state of matter that is produced in a mineral oil refining process. It consists mainly of carbon and can be uses as a fuel.

Photon.meaning: A photon is a material entity that is a light particle.

Plutonium.meaning: Plutonium is a portion of matter with the chemical formula Pu. It has a solid normal state of matter.

Primärenergieträger.meaning: A primary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the disposition primary energy carrier disposition.

PtL-Kraftstoff.meaning: PtL fuel is a liquid synthetic fuel produced in a power-to-liquid system from water and carbon dioxide using electrical energy.

Raffineriegas.meaning: Refinery gas is a gas mixture that is produced as a by-product of a mineral oil refining process. It mainly consists of hydrogen, methane, ethane and olefins and can be used as a fuel.

Rohöl.meaning: Crude oil is a portion of mater of fossil origin comprising a mixture of hydrocarbons and associated impurities, such as sulphur. It exists in the liquid phase under normal surface temperature and pressure and its physical characteristics (density, viscosity, etc.) are highly variable. This category includes field or lease condensate recovered from associated and non-associated gas where it is commingled with the commercial crude oil stream.

Sekundärenergieträger.meaning: A secondary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the secondary energy carrier disposition.

Siedlungsabfälle.meaning: Siedlungsabfälle: Abfallbrennstoff aus Haushalten oder nicht-industriellen gewerblichen Tätigkeiten.

Solarthermie.meaning: Solarthermie: Wärmeenergie, die als Ergebnis einer solarthermischen Energieumwandlung entsteht.

Sonstige.meaning: Etwas, das keiner der übrigen Einträge dieser Liste ist.

Stadtgas.meaning:
Gasworks gas is manufactured coal based gas that covers all types of gases produced in public utility or private plants, whose main purpose is manufacture, transport and distribution of gas. It includes gas produced by carbonisation (including gas produced by coke ovens and transferred to gasworks gas), by total gasification with or without enrichment with oil products (LPG, residual fuel oil, etc.), and by reforming and simple mixing of gases and/or air, reported under the rows ‘from other sources’. Under the transformation sector identify amounts of gasworks gas transferred to blended natural gas which will be distributed and consumed through the natural gas grid.

The production of other coal gases (i.e. coke oven gas, blast furnace gas and oxygen steel furnace gas) should be reported in the columns concerning such gases, and not as production of gasworks gas. The coal gases transferred to gasworks plants should then be reported (in their own column) in the transformation sector in the gasworks plants row. The total amount of gasworks gas resulting from transfers of other coal gases should appear in the production line for gasworks gas.

Steinkohle.meaning: Steinkohle: Kohle mit einem Brennwert über 23 865 kJ/kg und einer mittleren Vitrinitreflexion von mindestens 0,6.

Strom.meaning: Elektrische Energie aus geladenen Teilchen, unterscheidet sich als nicht-materieller Energieträger.

Summe.meaning: Die Zahl gilt für alle Energieträger zusammen: ihre Zeile oder Spalte summiert ausdrücklich über die Energieträger, oder ihre eigene Tabelle oder ihr Satz ist gar nicht nach Energieträgern aufgeteilt, nur nach anderem (Gebäudetyp, Sektor, Gebiet). Der Wärmebedarf der Gebäude eines Gebiets bleibt Summe, solange die Stelle nicht nach Energieträgern aufteilt.

Synthesegas.meaning: Syngas is a gas mixture consisting primarily of hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and very often carbon dioxide, that can be used as fuel.

Thorium.meaning: Thorium is a portion of matter with the chemical formula Th. It has a solid normal state of matter.

Torf.meaning: Peat is a or portion of matter that is a soft, porous or compressed, sedimentary deposit of plant origin with high water content (up to 90 % in the raw state) and can be used as combustion fuel. As the natural formation of peat takes at least centuries, peat is usually considered having a fossil origin.

Umweltwärme.meaning: In Luft, Erde oder Wasser gespeicherte Wärme, die durch Wärmepumpen genutzt wird.

Uran.meaning: Uranium is a portion of matter that has the atomic number 92. It is a silver-grey metal.

Verbrennungsbrennstoff.meaning: A combustion fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by chemical reaction with other substances.

Wasser.meaning: Water is a portion of matter with the chemical formula H2O. It has a liquid normal state of matter.

Wasserstoff.meaning: Wasserstoff: Stoff mit der chemischen Formel H2, der gasförmig vorliegt und als Brennstoff verwendet werden kann.

Wasserstoff aus Dampfreformierung.meaning: Steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is a physical output of a steam reforming process.

Wasserstoff aus Dampfreformierung mit CO.meaning: Abated steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is output of a steam reforming process which is followed by a carbon capture and storage process.

Wasserstoff aus Methanpyrolyse.meaning: Methane pyrolytic hydrogen is synthetic hydrogen that is produced from pyrolysis of methane and solid CO2 storage.

West Texas Intermediate.meaning: Western Texas Intermediate (WTI) is a crude oil that is extracted on US territory and traded at NYMEX New York.

biogener Festbrennstoff.meaning: Biogener Festbrennstoff: Organisches, nicht fossiles Material biologischen Ursprungs, das zur Wärme- oder Stromerzeugung genutzt werden kann.

biogener Industrieabfallbrennstoff.meaning: A biogenic industrial waste fuel is an industrial waste fuel that has a biogenic origin.

biogener Siedlungsabfall.meaning: Siedlungsabfall mit biogenem Ursprung, unterscheidet sich durch die biologische Herkunft.

erneuerbarer Brennstoff.meaning: A renewable fuel is a fuel that has a renewable origin and an renewable energy carrier disposition

erneuerbarer Elektrolysewasserstoff.meaning: Renewable electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with renewable electrical energy.

erneuerbarer Energieträger.meaning: A renewable energy carrier is an energy carrier that has a renewable energy carrier disposition.

fester Brennstoff.meaning: A solid combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

fester erneuerbarer Brennstoff.meaning: A solid renewable fuel is a renewable fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

fester fossiler Brennstoff.meaning: A solid fossil fuel is a fossil fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiger Biobrennstoff.meaning: A liquid biofuel is a biofuel that has liquid as its normal state of matter.

flüssiger synthetischer Brennstoff.meaning: A liquid synthetic fuel is a synthetic fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

flüssiges Wasser.meaning: Liquid water is water that has a liquid state of matter.

fossiler Siedlungsabfall.meaning: A fossil municipal waste fuel is an municipal waste fuel that has a fossil origin.

fossiler Wasserstoff aus Dampfreformieru.meaning: Fossil steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is produced from a fossil combustion fuel in a steam reforming process which is not followed by a carbon capture and storage process.

gasförmiger Brennstoff.meaning: A gaseous combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a gaseous state of matter under normal conditions.

gasförmiger fossiler Brennstoff.meaning: A gaseous fossil fuel is a fossil combustion fuel that has a gaseous state of matter under normal conditions.

hochgepumptes Wasser.meaning: Pumped water is liquid water which was pumped into an upper reservoir and thus contains potential energy.

industrielle Abwärme.meaning: Industrielle Abwärme: Abwärme, die als Energieausgabe eines industriellen Prozesses entsteht.

komprimiertes Biomethan.meaning: Compressed biomethane is biomethane that has been compressed.

komprimiertes Erdgas (CNG).meaning: Compressed natural gas (CNG) is natural gas that has been compressed.

komprimiertes synthetisches Methan.meaning: Compressed synthetic methane is synthetic methane that has been compressed.

landwirtschaftlicher Abfallbrennstoff.meaning: Landwirtschaftlicher Abfallbrennstoff: Abfallbrennstoff aus der Landwirtschaft.

nachhaltiger Biobrennstoff.meaning: A sustainable biofuel is a biofuel that does conform to sustainability criteria.

natürliche Umweltwärme.meaning: Umweltwärme mit erneuerbarem Ursprung, unterscheidet sich durch natürliche Herkunft.

nicht nachhaltiger Biobrennstoff.meaning: A non-sustainable biofuel is a biofuel that does not conform to sustainability criteria.

spaltbares Material.meaning: A fissile material entity is a material entity that has the disposition to carry nuclear (binding) energy.

synthetischer Brennstoff.meaning: A synthetic fuel is a fuel produced from one or more portion(s) of matter using electric energy.

synthetischer Wasserstoff.meaning: Synthetic hydrogen is hydrogen with synthetic origin.

parameter.x-description-source: Eine im Wärmeplan bilanzierte Energiemenge, je Energieträger, Sektor und Jahr. Welche Größe es ist, wählst du in "quantity" aus der Liste. Die Ontologie definiert die beiden Klassen so: final energy consumption value ist "the energy delivered to and consumed by end users". Darunter fällt BEIDES, was ein deutscher Wärmeplan Verbrauch nennt und was er Bedarf nennt: für ein Zielszenario ist nichts gemessen, jede Zahl ist gerechnet, und die Definition spricht nicht von Messung. Ein Wärmebedarf, ein Endenergiebedarf und ein zu deckender Wärmebedarf sind also diese Klasse. primary energy consumption value ist "the total consumption of energy in a spatial region excluding the non-energetic use of fuels", also die Bilanz vor der Umwandlung. Ein Potenzial ist "a maximum value that describes some upper limit in a spatial region of reference", also ein erschließbares Maximum und keine verbrauchte Menge. Die Ontologie unterscheidet theoretisches, technisches (technological), wirtschaftliches (economic), erschließbares (developable) und nachhaltiges (sustainable) Potenzial, jeweils als flow potential (eine Menge je Zeit) oder als stock potential (ein Bestand, etwa eine Speichermenge). Wähle die Art, die die Quelle druckt; nennt sie keine Art, wähle flow potential für eine Menge je Zeit (etwa MWh/a), stock potential für einen Bestand und potential nur, wenn auch das offen ist. Jede Zahl mit einer Energieeinheit ist nach der Ontologie ein energy value, "a quantity value that has an energy unit as unit": auch eine Erzeugung, eine Nutzenergie oder eine Einsparung. Die Liste trägt alle Klassen der Ontologie darunter; wähle die genaueste, deren Definition die Zahl trifft. Die Einträge out: sind Zahlen, für die die Ontologie keine Klasse hat, etwa ein Wert je Einwohner. Das ist ein richtiges Ergebnis, kein Fehler.
parameter.x-question: Um WELCHE Kennzahl handelt es sich bei dieser Zahl? Entscheide danach, was die Quelle über sie sagt: die Einheit, die Spalten- oder Zeilenbeschriftung und die Tabellen- oder Abschnittsüberschrift. Eine Angabe in t CO2 ist eine Emission, eine Angabe in MWh oder GWh ein Energieverbrauch. Zitiere die Stelle, aus der das hervorgeht. Eine Angabe in kW, MW oder GW ist eine Leistung. Eine Angabe in % ist ein Anteil. Eine Zahl von Gebäuden ist eine Gebäudeanzahl.

Abfallbrennstoff.meaning: Brennstoff, bei dem das Material Abfall ist, umfasst alle Abfallarten.

Abwärme.meaning: Abwärme: Wärmeenergie, die bei einem Energieumwandlungsprozess entsteht und ungenutzt an die Umwelt abgegeben wird.

Ammoniak.meaning: Ammonia is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NH3. It has a gaseous normal state of matter and can act as an air pollutant. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Anthrazit.meaning: Anthracite is a hard coal with a high caloric value due to its high carbon content (about 90 % fixed carbon).

B7.meaning: B7 is a diesel fuel that consists of fossil diesel fuel and up to 7 % biodiesel and that is liquid.

Benzin.meaning: Gasoline (American English) or petrol (British English) is a portion of matter in the form of a transparent petroleum-derived liquid that is used primarily as a fuel in spark-ignited internal combustion engines. It consists mostly of organic compounds obtained by the fractional distillation of petroleum, enhanced with a variety of additives.

Bio-Ottokraftstoff.meaning: Biogasoline is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a gasoline fuel role. It consists of bioethanol, biomethanol and products of these two substances. It is made from vegetable or animal material and thus has a biogenic origin.

Biobrennstoff.meaning: A biofuel is a combustion fuel that has a biogenic origin.

Biodiesel.meaning: Biodiesel is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a diesel fuel role. It is produced from plants or animals and thus has a biogenic origin.

Bioethanol.meaning: Bioethanol is ethanol with a biogenic origin.

Biogas.meaning: Biogas: Durch anaerobe Vergärung entstehendes Gasgemisch aus hauptsächlich Methan und Kohlendioxid, das als Brennstoff dient.

Biomasse.meaning: Biomasse: Stoff pflanzlichen oder tierischen Ursprungs und damit biogener Herkunft.

Biomethan.meaning: Biomethan: Aus Biogas durch Abtrennung von Kohlendioxid gewonnenes Gasgemisch aus hauptsächlich Methan, das als Brennstoff dient.

Braunkohle.meaning: Braunkohle: Nicht backende Kohle mit einem Brennwert unter 17 435 kJ/kg und über 31 % flüchtigen Bestandteilen.

Brennstoff.meaning: A fuel is a portion of matter that has the disposition to be an energy carrier and that has a fuel role.

Brent-Rohöl.meaning: Brent crude is a crude oil that is extracted in the North Sea and traded at ICE London.

Dampf.meaning: Steam is water that has a gaseous state of matter.

Dieselkraftstoff.meaning: A diesel fuel is a combustion fuel that has a diesel fuel role.

Druckgaskraftstoff.meaning: A compressed gas fuel is a combustion fuel that has a compressed gas fuel role.

Druckluft.meaning: Compressed air is air that has been compressed to store energy. To discharge energy, the air is expanded.

Düsenkraftstoff.meaning: Jet fuel is kerosene used for aviation turbine power units. It has the same distillation characteristics between 150 °C and 300 °C (generally not above 250 °C) and flash point as kerosene. In addition, it has particular specifications (such as freezing point) which are established by the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

E10.meaning: E10 is a gasoline fuel that consists of (fossil) gasoline and up to 10 % ethanol and that is liquid.

Elektrolysewasserstoff.meaning: Electrolytic hydrogen is hydrogen that is a physical output of a water electrolysis process.

Elektrolysewasserstoff aus Kernenergie.meaning: Nuclear electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with nuclear electrical energy.

Elektrolysewasserstoff aus Solarstrom.meaning: Solar electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with solar electrical energy.

Endenergieträger.meaning: A final energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the disposition final energy carrier disposition.

Erdgas.meaning: Erdgas: Gasgemisch aus unterirdischen Lagerstätten, das hauptsächlich aus Methan besteht.

Erdgas aus reinen Gasfeldern.meaning: Non associated gas is natural gas originating from fields producing hydrocarbons only in gaseous form.

Erdölbegleitgas.meaning: Associated gas is a natural gas that is a byproduct from crude oil exploitation.

Ethanol.meaning: Ethanol is a portion of matter with the chemical formula C2H6O. It has a liquid normal state of matter and can be used as a combustion fuel.

Ethen.meaning: Ethene, or colloquially Ethylene, is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula H2C=CH2. It is gaseous in its normal state and can be used as a combustion fuel.

Fernwärme.meaning: Fernwärme: Leitungsgebundene Wärmelieferung an Wohn- oder Gewerbegebäude.

Flugbenzin.meaning: Aviation gasoline is gasoline used as motor spirit and prepared especially for aviation piston engines, with an octane number suited to the engine, a freezing point of -60 °C and a distillation range usually within the limits of 30 °C and 180 °C.

Fluss.meaning: A river is a water body that moves through permanent or seasonal flow process from elevated land towards lower elevations through a definite channel and empties either into a sea, lake, or another river or ends on land as bed seepage and evapotranspiration exceed water supply.

Flüssiggas.meaning: Flüssiggasgemisch aus Propan und Butan, unterscheidet sich als fossiler Gasbrennstoff.

Flüssigluft.meaning: Liquid air is air that has a liquid state of matter.

Gas aus Kohle.meaning: A manufactured coal based gas is a gas mixture that is manufactured from coal. It is used as fossil fuel.

Gasöl.meaning: Gas/diesel oil is a portion of matter that is primarily a medium distillate distilling between 180 °C and 380 °C. Includes blending components. Several grades are available depending on uses.

Geothermie.meaning: Geothermie: Wärmeenergie, die aus dem Inneren der Erdkruste freigesetzt wird.

Gestein.meaning: A rock is a portion of matter that is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter that is part of the earth's crust.

Gewässer.meaning: A water body is an accumulation of liquid water of varying size on the surface of the Earth.

Gichtgas.meaning: Blast furnace gas is manufactured coal based gas produced during the combustion of coke in blast furnaces in the iron and steel industry. It is recovered and used as a fuel partly within the plant and partly in other steel industry processes or in power stations equipped to burn it. The quantity of fuel should be reported on a gross calorific value basis.

Grubengas.meaning: Colliery gas is natural gas found in coal mines (British English: colliery). The main component is methane. Synonyms are firedamp, mine gas. It is used as a fossil fuel.

Heizöl.meaning: Heizöl: Gasöl für industrielle und gewerbliche Zwecke, auch schwere Gasöle, die als petrochemische Rohstoffe dienen.

Holz.meaning: Holz: Biomasse von Bäumen in festem Aggregatzustand, die als Brennstoff genutzt werden kann.

Holzkohle.meaning: Charcoal is a portion of matter produced from wood via pyrolysis. It has a solid state of matter and can be used as fuel.

Industrieabfallbrennstoff.meaning: An industrial waste fuel is waste fuel produced by industry.

Kernbrennstoff.meaning: A nuclear fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by undergoing nuclear fission.

Kerosin.meaning:
Kerosene, also known as paraffin, lamp oil, and coal oil (an obsolete term), is a portion of matter consisting of combustible hydrocarbon liquid which is derived from petroleum. It is widely used as a fuel in industry as well as households. It is sometimes spelled kerosine in scientific and industrial usage.
[...]

Kerosene is widely used to power jet engines of aircraft (jet fuel) and some rocket engines and is also commonly used as a cooking and lighting fuel and for fire toys such as poi. In parts of Asia, kerosene is sometimes used as fuel for small outboard motors or even motorcycles.

Kohle.meaning: Kohle: Brennbares schwarzes bis schwarzbraunes Sedimentgestein, das in Flözen entstanden ist.

Kohleabraum.meaning: Coal refuse is a fossil waste fuel that is the material left over from coal mining. It can partially be reused as fuel.

Kohlenwasserstoff.meaning: Hydrocarbon is a portion of matter which is member of class of organic chemical compounds composed only of the elements carbon (C) and hydrogen (H).

Kokereigas.meaning: Coke oven gas is manufactured coal based gas obtained as a by-product of the manufacture of coke oven coke for the production of iron and steel.

Kokskohle.meaning: Coking coal is hard coal that is bituminous with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is greater than 23 865 kJ/kg (5 700 kcal/kg) on an ash-free but moist basis.

Luft.meaning: Air is a gas mixture that forms the Earth's atmosphere.

Methan.meaning: Methane is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH4. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It occurs naturally in the atmosphere as a trace gas and can work as a greenhouse gas. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Methanol.meaning: Methanol is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH3OH. It has a liquid normal state of matter. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

Mineralöl.meaning: A mineral oil is a fossil combustion fuel that is either crude oil or a mineral oil product.

Mineralölprodukt.meaning: A mineral oil product is a fossil combustion fuel produced in a mineral oil refining process.

Mischkraftstoff.meaning: A blended liquid fuel is a liquid combustion fuel that contains a liquid fossil fuel and a liquid renewable fuel or a liquid biofuel.

Motorenbenzin.meaning:
Motor gasoline is gasoline consisting of a mixture of light hydrocarbons distilling between 35 °C and 215 °C. It is used as a fuel for land based spark ignition engines. Motor gasoline may include additives, oxygenates and octane enhancers, including lead compounds such as TEL and TML.

Includes motor gasoline blending components (excluding additives/oxygenates), e.g. alkylates, isomerate, reformate, cracked gasoline destined for use as finished motor gasoline.

Ottokraftstoff.meaning: A gasoline fuel is a combustion fuel that has a gasoline fuel role.

Ozean.meaning: The ocean is a water body that consists of salt water and is covering approximately 71% of Earth's surface.

Petrolkoks.meaning: Petroleum coke is a portion of matter with a solid state of matter that is produced in a mineral oil refining process. It consists mainly of carbon and can be uses as a fuel.

Photon.meaning: A photon is a material entity that is a light particle.

Plutonium.meaning: Plutonium is a portion of matter with the chemical formula Pu. It has a solid normal state of matter.

Primärenergieträger.meaning: A primary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the disposition primary energy carrier disposition.

PtL-Kraftstoff.meaning: PtL fuel is a liquid synthetic fuel produced in a power-to-liquid system from water and carbon dioxide using electrical energy.

Raffineriegas.meaning: Refinery gas is a gas mixture that is produced as a by-product of a mineral oil refining process. It mainly consists of hydrogen, methane, ethane and olefins and can be used as a fuel.

Rohöl.meaning: Crude oil is a portion of mater of fossil origin comprising a mixture of hydrocarbons and associated impurities, such as sulphur. It exists in the liquid phase under normal surface temperature and pressure and its physical characteristics (density, viscosity, etc.) are highly variable. This category includes field or lease condensate recovered from associated and non-associated gas where it is commingled with the commercial crude oil stream.

Sekundärenergieträger.meaning: A secondary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the secondary energy carrier disposition.

Siedlungsabfälle.meaning: Siedlungsabfälle: Abfallbrennstoff aus Haushalten oder nicht-industriellen gewerblichen Tätigkeiten.

Solarthermie.meaning: Solarthermie: Wärmeenergie, die als Ergebnis einer solarthermischen Energieumwandlung entsteht.

Sonstige.meaning: Etwas, das keiner der übrigen Einträge dieser Liste ist.

Stadtgas.meaning:
Gasworks gas is manufactured coal based gas that covers all types of gases produced in public utility or private plants, whose main purpose is manufacture, transport and distribution of gas. It includes gas produced by carbonisation (including gas produced by coke ovens and transferred to gasworks gas), by total gasification with or without enrichment with oil products (LPG, residual fuel oil, etc.), and by reforming and simple mixing of gases and/or air, reported under the rows ‘from other sources’. Under the transformation sector identify amounts of gasworks gas transferred to blended natural gas which will be distributed and consumed through the natural gas grid.

parameter.x-description-source: Eine im Wärmeplan angegebene Leistung, also Energie je Zeit: eine Heizlast, eine Anschlussleistung, eine Netz- oder Erzeugerleistung, die Nennwärmeleistung eines Kessels oder BHKW. Welche Größe es ist, wählst du in "quantity" aus der Liste. Die Ontologie definiert die Klasse über ihre Einheit: power value ist "a quantity value that has a power unit as unit", also jede Angabe in kW, MW oder GW. Die Einheit trennt diesen Parameter von den anderen: kW gegen kWh. Eine Angabe in kWh, MWh oder GWh ist KEINE Leistung, sondern eine Energiemenge, auch wenn die Zeile das Wort Leistung enthält. Eine ANZAHL (Gebäude, Anlagen, Anschlüsse) ist keine Leistung und hat keine Einheit dieser Liste, auch wenn sie in derselben Zeile steht; eine Zahl von Gebäuden ist eine Gebäudeanzahl. Ein Leistungspotenzial ist ein Potenzial, "a maximum value that describes some upper limit in a spatial region of reference", also eine erschließbare und keine bereitgestellte Leistung. Die Ontologie unterscheidet theoretisches, technisches (technological), wirtschaftliches (economic), erschließbares (developable) und nachhaltiges (sustainable) Potenzial, jeweils als flow potential (eine Menge je Zeit) oder als stock potential (ein Bestand, etwa eine Speichermenge). Eine Leistung ist Energie je Zeit: wähle die Art, die die Quelle druckt, und nennt sie keine Art, flow potential. Die Einträge out: sind Größen ohne Klasse der Ontologie. Wähle den passenden davon, wenn die Zahl eine davon ist. Das ist ein richtiges Ergebnis, kein Fehler.
parameter.x-question: Um WELCHE Kennzahl handelt es sich bei dieser Zahl? Entscheide danach, was die Quelle über sie sagt: die Einheit, die Spalten- oder Zeilenbeschriftung und die Tabellen- oder Abschnittsüberschrift. Eine Angabe in t CO2 ist eine Emission, eine Angabe in MWh oder GWh ein Energieverbrauch. Zitiere die Stelle, aus der das hervorgeht. Eine Angabe in kW, MW oder GW ist eine Leistung. Eine Angabe in % ist ein Anteil. Eine Zahl von Gebäuden ist eine Gebäudeanzahl.

parameter.x-description-source: Eine Organisation, die die Wärmeplanung erstellt hat: das beauftragte Ingenieur-, Planungs- oder Beratungsbüro und die Kommune oder Behörde, die den Plan als planungsverantwortliche Stelle erstellt. Ein Tupel je Organisation, in der Schreibweise des Dokuments, ohne Rechtsform. Zu finden im Impressum, auf der Titelseite, unter Auftraggeber, Auftragnehmer, Bearbeitung, Erstellt durch oder Verfasser. NICHT Fördermittelgeber, Datenlieferanten, Netzbetreiber oder im Text erwähnte Firmen: sie erstellen den Plan nicht.
parameter.x-question: Um WELCHE Kennzahl handelt es sich bei dieser Zahl? Entscheide danach, was die Quelle über sie sagt: die Einheit, die Spalten- oder Zeilenbeschriftung und die Tabellen- oder Abschnittsüberschrift. Eine Angabe in t CO2 ist eine Emission, eine Angabe in MWh oder GWh ein Energieverbrauch. Zitiere die Stelle, aus der das hervorgeht. Eine Angabe in kW, MW oder GW ist eine Leistung. Eine Angabe in % ist ein Anteil. Eine Zahl von Gebäuden ist eine Gebäudeanzahl.
